definitions.definition: An AI system is a machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. Different AI systems vary in their levels of autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment.

note: The stored print is the Compendium of OECD Legal Instruments entry (OECD/LEGAL/0449, adopted 22/05/2019, amended 03/05/2024). Its background information says the Council revised the definition of an AI system on 8 November 2023; the quoted text is the current one. 'Artificial intelligence' is only abbreviated in the preamble ('hereafter, “AI”'), not defined. Paragraph I also defines 'AI system lifecycle', 'AI actors', 'AI knowledge' and 'stakeholders', which have no term group in this pilot. 'Generative AI' is mentioned only in the background information. The Recommendation also exists in French; only the English text is stored.
